svg.title: Order for coordinating two Canadian workplace benefit plans
svg.desc: Your own plan pays your claim first. A child's claim follows the birthday rule, then the second plan with the explanation of benefits. A health spending account is last. Combined payment cannot exceed 100 percent of the eligible expense. Not a quote.
svg.text: Who pays, and in what order
CLHIA coordination order. Not a way to pick the richer plan first. 24 Sep 2026.
1. Your own employee plan, for your claim
2. Child: earlier birthday in the year
3. Second plan, with the first EOB
4. Health spending account, if the booklet pays after both insured plans
Stop at 100 percent of the eligible expense. A billed fee above reasonable and customary can stay unpaid.
Joint custody uses the biological parents' birthdays first. A step-parent plan does not jump ahead.
Quebec RAMQ-eligible student drug claims are an exception: the parent's plan pays those first.
Same month and day: first names in alphabetical order. Year of birth does not decide.
